measurement: Each query has author-written expectations (written from knowledge of the texts BEFORE the first run; any later change is recorded in 'revised'). A query PASSES when every stated expectation holds. hit@10 = share of queries with a 'verses' expectation whose expected verse(s) appear in the first 10 results (all of them when mode is 'all', one of them when 'any'). MRR@25 = mean over the same queries of 1/rank of the first expected verse among the first 25 results (0 if absent). These measure whether specific, known verses are found; they are NOT a general relevance score and the set is small (author-chosen, not sampled from real users).
